---
title: "User guide"
---

The guide follows the path from raw observations to a possession-level risk profile. All examples use observed match data and the models distributed with PRESS.

1. **[Datasets, installation and preprocessing](data.qmd).** Obtain the SkillCorner files, install PRESS, load a match and inspect the prepared input tables.
2. **[Possession segmentation and context](vignettes/setup/possession_and_checkpoint_setup.ipynb).** Understand individual and team possessions, canonical actions, checkpoints and context labels.
3. **[Use on a match](vignettes/00_match_workflow/00_match_workflow.ipynb).** Navigate a real match, calculate h and xLoss, plot frames and checkpoints, and save and reload results.
4. **Use with other providers.**
   - [4.1 · Data requirements and preparation](external-data.qmd) defines the input contract and synchronization/segmentation workflow.
   - [4.2 · Bundesliga example](vignettes/00_external_data/idsse.ipynb) applies it to Köln–Bayern.

The SkillCorner loader in part 1 prepares the original match files in memory. For another provider, follow part 4 to map and align the data before initializing PRESS. Individual possessions can be reconstructed through the segmentation interface; PRESS then constructs canonical actions and checkpoints.

The four-part [reference](api.qmd) documents individual classes and functions: [initialization](api.qmd), [solvers](solvers.qmd), [getters](reference/getters.qmd) and [plots](reference/plots.qmd). The [model pages](index.qmd#models) explain the mathematical components; the [benchmarks](benchmark.qmd) describe their training and held-out evaluation.

[Models, calculation configurations and frame results](api.qmd#model-configuration-result) explains where fitted coefficients, spline designs, physical settings and predictions are stored, with ball-drive, pitch-control and BCOS examples.
